title: utv for Python deployment diagram
description: How the library reaches a program: a setuptools package that the application's own Python interpreter imports and runs in-process, given zone rules the application loads. Nothing in the repository publishes it to a package index or tags a release of it; the repository's tests import it from src/ with PYTHONPATH=src.

nodes.name: Python 3.10+ interpreter
nodes.description: The interpreter the application runs in (pyproject.toml: requires-python >= 3.10).

nodes.name: Application process
nodes.description: The application developer's program. It imports utv and calls it; every operation is an in-process function call with no I/O of its own.

nodes.name: Host tz database
nodes.description: The tz data zoneinfo reads for a ZoneInfo the application constructs. utv never opens it; utv.native only calls utcoffset and astimezone on such a ZoneInfo.
nodes.condition: Only when the application passes a ZoneInfo, or a datetime carrying one, to from_native or to_native.

artifacts.name: utv 0.3.0
artifacts.description: The package built by setuptools from src/utv, standard library only (dependencies = []).

artifacts.name: Bundled schema
artifacts.description: Package data (data/*.json), read at run time by validate_structural through importlib.resources.

artifacts.name: Zone-rule bundle
artifacts.description: Rule data the application loads with ZoneRules.load(path) or ZoneRules.parse(text) and holds in a TemporalContext. The package ships none; this demo bundle (three zones, 2026–2027) is the only one in the repository and is what the tests use.

relationships.description: Runs the application, and utv inside it.
Through zoneinfo.ZoneInfo objects the application creates.
